title: ARMS AND GENTLE CORE
subtitle: SEATED FIRST, THEN STANDING AT THE WALL AND CHAIR. NO FLOOR TODAY. KIND HIPS.

script.welcome: Good morning Pam. I'm Stratton. Friday is arms and gentle core, about ten minutes. We start in the chair with a tummy-switched-on march, rows, and an easy overhead reach, then we stand for wall push ups, a kind hip flexor stretch, and a touch of balance at the chair. No floor today. A smaller range is fine on sore-joint days. Well done for showing up.
script.start: Whenever you're ready. Sit tall near the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat, shoulders soft, easy breath.
script.nextExercise: Next one. Settle in. No rush.
script.lastSet: Last one of these. Keep it comfortable.
script.complete: That's us, Pam. Arms worked, tummy switched on, hips looked after, and a proper little break from the desk. Have a sip of water and enjoy your Friday. Well done.
script.pause: Paused. Take all the time you need.
script.resume: Back with you. Easy as we go.

exercises.name: SEATED MARCH WITH GENTLE BRACE
exercises.cue: Sit tall near the front of the chair, hands resting on the seat edge. Draw the belly button gently in, as if zipping up snug trousers, and keep breathing. March slowly in place, lifting one knee a few inches, then the other, without leaning back. Slow and tall is the core work. Small lifts are plenty. If the front of the left hip pinches, lift the left knee only a little, or just raise the left heel instead. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness.
exercises.speakStart: Seated march with a gentle brace. Two bursts of about twenty seconds. Sit tall, tummy gently in, keep breathing, and lift one knee a few inches, then the other, nice and slow. Keep the left lift small if the hip grumbles.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Feet flat. Let the tummy relax.
exercises.speakDone: March done. Lovely, the core is awake.

exercises.name: SEATED ROW
exercises.cue: Sit tall, feet flat. Reach both arms forward at chest height, empty hands or very light weights. Draw the elbows back close to the ribs and gently squeeze the shoulder blades together, pause, then reach forward again. Slow and controlled. Keep the shoulders down away from the ears. Empty hands are always fine, and a smaller pull is fine on sore-joint days.
exercises.speakStart: Seated row. Two sets of eight. Reach forward, draw the elbows back, gentle squeeze between the shoulder blades, little pause. Empty hands are perfect.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Arms down. Shoulders soft.

exercises.name: SEATED OVERHEAD REACH
exercises.cue: Sit tall, feet flat, tummy gently in so the back stays tall. Start with hands at shoulder height, palms forward, empty or holding very light weights. Press up toward the ceiling as far as is comfortable, then lower slowly back to the shoulders. No need to lock the elbows or reach all the way up; stop where the shoulders feel happy. Keep the ribs soft and do not arch the back.
exercises.speakStart: Seated overhead reach. Two sets of six. Hands at the shoulders, tummy gently in, reach up only as high as feels kind, then slowly back down. Empty hands are fine.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Hands in the lap. Breathe.
exercises.speakDone: Overhead reach done. Now stand up from the chair nice and slowly, use your hands, take your time, and step over to the wall.

exercises.name: WALL PUSH-UPS
exercises.cue: Stand facing the wall, about an arm's length away, feet hip-width. Place the hands flat on the wall at shoulder height, a little wider than the shoulders. Keep the body in one long line from head to heels, tummy gently in. Bend the elbows to bring the chest toward the wall, then press back. Stand closer to make it easier; a small bend is plenty on sore-joint days. Keep the wrists comfortable.
exercises.speakStart: Wall push ups. Two sets of six. Hands on the wall at shoulder height, body long, tummy gently in. Bend the elbows toward the wall, then press away. Step closer if you want it easier.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Hands off the wall. Shake the arms out.
exercises.speakDone: Wall push ups done. Strong arms, Pam. Well done.

exercises.name: STANDING HIP FLEXOR
exercises.cue: Stand beside the chair with the right hand lightly on the chair back. Step the left foot back about half a step, not a deep lunge, both feet pointing forward, knees soft. Gently tuck the pelvis under (belt buckle toward the ribs) until you feel a mild stretch at the front of the left hip. A tiny lean is enough. Breathe slowly for about twenty seconds. Small and kind, never aggressive. A lovely undo for all the sitting. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness.
exercises.speakStart: Standing hip flexor, left leg back. Two holds of about twenty seconds. Small step back, pelvis tucked, tiny lean. Kind and small.
exercises.speakRest: Fifteen seconds. Feet together. Easy breath.

exercises.name: CHAIR BALANCE
exercises.cue: Stand behind or beside the sturdy chair with one or both hands on the chair back. Stand tall, tummy gently in. Shift your weight onto one foot and lift the other heel, or the whole foot just an inch, for about fifteen seconds. Then switch sides. Eyes on a fixed point ahead, breathe. Hold the chair as firmly as you need. If the left hip grumbles when standing on it, keep the toes of the other foot lightly touching the floor. Stop if anything feels sharp or wobbly in a worrying way.
exercises.speakStart: Chair balance to finish. About fifteen seconds each side. Hands on the chair, stand tall, lift one foot a little, eyes ahead. Hold on as much as you like.
exercises.speakRest: Ten seconds. Both feet down. Easy breath.
exercises.speakDone: Balance done. That's the session, Pam. Arms, core, and kind hips all looked after. Have a grand Friday.
